title: Rollout Ceremony Roles Matrix and Fidelity Checklist (draft)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This working doc is an operational-first artifact: a concise roles matrix, pre-rollout fidelity checklist, and lightweight ceremony script for cross-functional canaries and A/B exposures. It is intended for medium-complexity LLM features (rerankers, controlled generation, response-safety filters) where both behavioral fidelity and cost/latency trade-offs matter.

High level goals (quick):
- Ensure each rollout has a single accountable steward and named backups for each discipline.
- Make signal selection explicit (safety, quality, latency, cost) and map signals -> owners -> thresholds.
- Standardize minimal ceremonies (pre-check, kickoff, 1h post-check, 24h sweep, rollback decision).
- Provide a template for on-the-fly decisions when signals conflict.

Roles matrix (names are examples; replace per release):
- Release Steward (product): accountable for success, triage decisions, and external comms (example: Aisha Patel).
- Model/Serving Owner (eng-serving-runtime): responsible for model variant, routing config, fallbacks, capacity reserve (example: Jonah Li).
- Observability Lead (eng-observability): sets dashboards, alert thresholds, and owns immediate investigation (example: Marina Kovac).
- SRE / Oncall (sre): ensures infra health, coordinates scaling/escalation (example: Ethan Brooks).
- Safety/Trust Reviewer (safety): owns behavioral thresholds and manual QA for edge cases (example: Priya Srinivasan).
- Solutions / Sales Liaison (cs): ensures key customers are pre-notified and served (ad-hoc).
- Data Analyst (product-ops): computes A/B metrics and surfaces regression signals.

Each role - minimal responsibilities checklist:
- Release Steward: confirm hypothesis, approve slice selection, declare primary rollback metric, run kickoff.
- Model/Serving Owner: verify model compatibility, pre-warm KV cache, validate routing policies and fallback mapping.
- Observability Lead: publish pre-populated dashboard, sanity-check synthetic traffic, define 1h/24h thresholds.
- SRE: reserve capacity, test autoscale triggers in staging, document runbook contact info.
- Safety Reviewer: run batch eval on priority prompts, flag any egregious outputs, provide revert threshold.
- Data Analyst: create baseline slices, implement logging for sample IDs, prepare A/B analysis notebook.

Pre-rollout fidelity checklist (must be green for rollout to proceed):
- Hypothesis statement present and measurable (Y/N).
- Canary slice(s) defined (size, cohort, geo) and traffic gating configured (Y/N).
- Primary rollback metric declared (token-level latency / user-visible error / safety score).
- Dashboards: latency, cpu/gpu utilization, tail-latency p99.9, error budget burn rate, safety violation rate.
- Synthetic smoke tests run against canary model (including long-context prompts).
- KV/prefix caching behavior validated with realistic sequences.
- Billing/rate-limit guardrails set (alerts for >X tokens/min or >$Y/hour).
- Notifications plan drafted (Slack channel, on-call pager, escalation contacts).

Signal catalog and example thresholds (treat as templates):
- Latency p95: gating threshold +30% over baseline -> investigate; +50% -> pause.
- Error rate (5xx or model crash): >0.5% -> pause and rollback intent.
- Safety violations (manual QA or automated classifier): any single high-severity violation -> immediate pause and convene safety reviewer.
- Quality regressions (A/B product metric e.g., CTR or rerank NDCG): relative drop >2.5% at 95% CI over 24h -> rollback.
- Cost burn: >25% over forecasted spend for canary window -> throttled exposure and notify finance.

Ceremony timeline (lightweight):
- T-72h: announce intent to release, tag stakeholders, run final smoke tests.
- T-24h: stakeholder dry-run (1h), confirm dashboards and alerts.
- T-1h: final steward sign-off, lock freeze on unrelated deploys, pre-warm endpoints.
- T+0h: expose canary (binary flag or route slice). Quick 5–10m sanity checks by Observability + SRE.
- T+1h: structured assessment: 1h post-check, data analyst posts short note (green/yellow/red) to channel.
- T+24h: 24h sweep with full A/B metric report and safety QA summary. Decision: broaden / maintain / rollback.

Decision rule examples (if multiple signals disagree):
- Safety violations (any): act as veto -> immediate pause and manual investigation.
- Latency severe (p95>2x baseline): if user-facing, pause; if internal batch, consider slower rollout.
- Quality small regressions (<3%): keep running and observe additional slices; require confirmatory signals from at least 2 independent metrics before rollback.
- Cost blowout: throttle slice to 10% and re-evaluate with finance.

Communication templates (brief snippets for Slack/Email):
- Pre-rollout: "Planned canary for <feature>. Steward: <name>. Canary slice: <size>. Primary rollback metric: <metric>. Start: <time>"
- 1h post: "1h canary check: latency p95 +5% vs baseline; errors 0.03%; quality delta +0.6% (green). Proceeding to 24h."
- Rollback notice: "Rolling back <feature> due to <primary reason>. Impacted slice: <ids>. Runbook: <link>."

Quick on-call runbook pointers (one-pagers):
- If model overloaded: shift traffic to fallback variant -> notify steward -> trigger autoscale if safe.
- If safety alert fires: snapshot logs, capture example IDs, escalate to safety reviewer, and pause exposure.
- If metric drift ambiguous: increase sampling to 100% for problematic cohort for 30 minutes and run quick manual checks.

Post-release artifacts (must produce):
- 24h A/B report (notebook + executive summary).
- Incident / interruption timeline if any (owner + timestamps).
- Lessons learned + changes to thresholds or signals.
- Updated roles matrix if person(s) rotated.

Open questions / TODO (working list):
- Who owns the formal approval to expand a canary >10% for features that affect cost? (product or finance?)
- Standardize safety severity taxonomy across teams (low/med/high) and map to automatic pause rules.
- Define maximum acceptable sample size for privacy-sensitive cohorts before needing legal review.
- Add a lightweight automation that posts a one-line canary summary to an internal dashboard channel.

Appendix: quick templates and checkboxes (copyable)
- Hypothesis: 
- Canary slice: 
- Primary rollback metric & threshold: 
- Dashboard links: 
- Stakeholders & escalation contacts: 
- Synthetic tests run: Y/N -> notes:

Notes to self (Aisha):
- Iterate on this after next 3 rollouts; capture friction points (especially ambiguous signal cases).
- Propose a small run-of-week ceremony for release stewards to align on thresholds and share prior incidents.

End of document.

(Informal: this is intentionally terse — meant to be copied into release ticket template and adapted per feature.)
